lines.say: Your friend hit send, and the message popped up on your screen instantly.
lines.show: Your friend hit *send,* and the message popped up on your screen *instantly.*

lines.say: You never pulled to refresh. So how did your phone know?
lines.show: You never pulled to refresh. So how did your phone [know?]

lines.say: Normally, your app asks the server something, and the server answers once. Want news? Ask again.
lines.show: Normally, your app *asks* the server something, and the server *answers* once. Want news? [Ask again.]

lines.say: In that setup, the server can't start a conversation. It only speaks when asked.
lines.show: In that setup, the server can't start a conversation. It [only speaks when asked.]

lines.say: A WebSocket keeps a line open between your phone and the server, like a call nobody hangs up.
lines.show: A *WebSocket* keeps a line *open* between your phone and the server, like a *call nobody hangs up.*

lines.say: Now either side can talk, any time. When your friend's message reaches the server, it sends it straight down the line to you.
lines.show: Now *either side* can talk, any time. When your friend's message reaches the server, it sends it *straight down the line* to you.

lines.say: One catch: every open line costs server memory. And if the connection breaks, your app has to reconnect.
lines.show: One catch: every open line costs [server memory.] And if the connection [breaks,] your app has to *reconnect.*

lines.say: Discord runs its live updates over WebSockets, and modern browsers support them too.
lines.show: *Discord* runs its live updates over WebSockets, and *modern browsers* support them too.

lines.say: If AI writes your code, follow for the system design it leaves out.
lines.show: If AI writes your code, *follow* for the system design it leaves out.
